author: IGN
description:
One Piece: Grand Gourmet reviewed by John Carson on Nintendo Switch 2, also available on Nintendo Switch and PC.

"Much like Monkey D. Luffy, One Piece: Grand Gourmet is a fairly carefree pirate collector that brushes off strategy in favor of brute force. Helping Sanji run a floating restaurant is a great premise, but the act of managing a sprawling mega-eatery loses its intrigue when it’s apparent how few decisions actually matter. Instead, most of the fun is simply in its fan service, getting to feed old friends and watch them interact with each other in amusing or unexpected ways that provide joy even past the credits. But unless you’re an established fan of the series or want a cute, mindless way to kill time, there’s no rush to climb aboard for this culinary voyage."

#IGN #Gaming
title: One Piece: Grand Gourmet Review

description:
After her baby brother is abducted by a murder of crows, headstrong teenager Prue McKeel (Peyton Elizabeth Lee) launches a desperate rescue mission into the Impassable Wilderness—an enchanted forest hidden just beyond Portland, Oregon. 

Joined by her hapless but loyal classmate Curtis Mehlberg (Jacob Tremblay), Prue navigates a world of talking animals, bandits, and powerful figures driven by grief and ambition. As the pair is drawn into a conflict threatening the balance of the forest itself, Prue must discover the strength and belief she never knew she possessed. If she hopes to save her brother and protect Wildwood’s fragile future, she will have to risk everything. 

From Oscar-nominated and BAFTA-winning LAIKA, Wildwood is a sweeping adventure about love, sacrifice, and the magic that reveals itself when we dare to look beyond the familiar. Wildwood, premieres October 23, 2026.

author: IGN
description:
The PlayStation 2 is the best-selling console of all time for well-documented reasons: its massive library, its headstart on the Xbox, its mid-life price cut, and its affordability as a DVD player. But the deal that brought a trio of Grand Theft Auto games – GTA 3, Vice City, and San Andreas – to the PS2 before any other platform was vital to it's success. They collectively make up three of its top six sellers. Some people bought the PS2 just to play GTA and if you didn't have one, you were nagging a friend who did.

We've heard snippets about this deal and about that key meeting at the Sunset Marquis before. But IGN has now spoken to four people at the centre of it all who can tell the story in more detail than ever. They reveal previously unknown twists and turns in negotiations: how Sony nearly missed out on exclusivity in the US, how Take Two got cash and a discount on production costs from Sony, and how Microsoft could've derailed the whole thing. This is how Sony secured GTA as
title: How Sony Secured GTA as a PS2 Exclusive

Don't miss the US Trailer for Bunker, a psychological thriller distributed by Sony Pictures Classics. Watch a couple navigate trying times in Bunker, in theaters January 15, 2027.

Bunker is a psychological thriller that examines the emotional and moral challenges faced by a couple in an increasingly uncertain world. Miguel, a successful London architect, considers a prestigious offer to build a survivalist bunker for a tech billionaire. This project causes his wife, Sofia, to question their relationship of 17 years as they are drawn deeper into a life of extreme wealth, paranoia, and fear. The intrusion of an unsettling neighbor becomes yet another source of anxiety.

Bunker stars Javier Bardem, Penélope Cruz, Stephen Graham, Patrick Schwarzenegger, and Paul Dano. The film is produced by Fernando Bovaira, Alice Dawson, Simón de Santiago, Federica Sainte-Rose, Florian Zeller, and Mariano Cohn.

Bunker is in theaters on January 15, 2027.
